item.title: The Efficiency of Typhoon Forecasts: Evidence from China's Public Typhoon Alert System
item.description: Weather and climate forecasting has spanned human history for thousands of years, with substantial improvements in accuracy driven by advances in meteorological science and numerical computational methods. As climate change has emerged as one of the central challenges of the 21st century, accompanied by increasingly frequent and intense weather-related natural disasters such as floods, typhoons, extreme temperatures, the importance of weather and climate forecasting has grown significantly. In low to mid latitude coastal regions, typhoons have posed recurring and severe risks to human lives and economic activities for thousands of years. The ability of scientific forecasting agencies to accurately predict cyclone paths and intensities, and the capacity of local governments to make timely decisions translating those predictions into public warnings, has become increasingly important for avoidance against typhoon damages in the populous and economically active coastal regions of Southern and Eastern China.
